$comment: Shared table for hdf-to-xml scalar number rendering. Go (scalarText) and TypeScript (formatJsonNumber) both read it, so neither language can drift. 'json' is the raw JSON number text the converter receives; 'text' is the canonical rendering emitted as XML character data. The canonical form is positional with shortest-round-trip digits and never exponent notation -- Go's strconv.FormatFloat(f, 'f', -1, 64) -- because it is what every shipped golden and the released CLI already emit, and because exponent notation in XML character data requires the reader to know the field is numeric.

cases.why: at the magnitude where JavaScript switches to exponent notation and Go does not
the same switch on the negative side
below the small-magnitude threshold where JavaScript switches to exponent
the same threshold on the negative side
significand carries a fraction, so the expansion is not just appended zeros
near the top of the double range: 309 digits positional
the smallest positive denormal, the longest positional form a double can produce
IEEE negative zero: Go keeps the sign bit, JavaScript's Number::toString drops it
one magnitude below the switch: both languages already agree, pinned so neither drifts
one magnitude above the small-side switch: both already agree
shortest round-trip drops the trailing zero in both languages
beyond 2^53: both languages lose the same bit, so they still agree
